entries.topic: Anti-boycott law, IHRA, EO 13899/14188, Antisemitism Awareness Act

claims.text: 1977 amendments to the Export Administration Act targeted US persons' compliance with unsanctioned foreign boycotts (EAA 1979 s.8, EAR Part 760); Ribicoff Amendment 1976 Tax Reform Act; Anti-Boycott Act of 2018 enacted 13 Aug 2018 in FY2019 NDAA as ECRA Part II; prohibitions on refusing to do business, furnishing information, discrimination; reporting requirement; Arab League boycott of Israel principal target; penalties up to $374,474 per violation administrative, $1m and 20 years criminal.

Carter signed H.R. 5840 (P.L. 95-52) on 22 Jun 1977, calling boycotts a 'profound moral issue', saying the law does not 'question the sovereign right of any nation to regulate its own commerce'; credited Business Roundtable, ADL, AJC, AJCongress and named members of Congress.

EO 13899 (11 Dec 2019): agencies enforcing Title VI 'shall consider' the IHRA working definition and contemporary examples; s.2(b) agencies 'shall not diminish or infringe upon' First Amendment rights; Title VI covers discrimination against Jews based on race, color or national origin.

EO 14188 (29 Jan 2025): reaffirms EO 13899; 60-day agency reports; recommendations to familiarize universities with inadmissibility grounds so they can monitor and report alien students and staff, which could lead to removal.
As of Aug 2024, 35 states plus DC used or recognized the IHRA definition; State Department used an earlier version from 2006.

IHRA definition text: 'criticism of Israel similar to that leveled against any other country cannot be regarded as antisemitic'; ADL calls it non-legally binding and opposes using it to create new categories of prohibited speech.

Kenneth Stern, lead drafter (2004–05), said in March 2025 the administration is 'absolutely weaponizing antisemitism'; White House replied 'the only people weaponizing antisemitism are the liberal activists'.

claims.text: EO 14203 (6 Feb 2025) cites 'illegitimate and baseless actions targeting America and our close ally Israel', the Netanyahu and Gallant warrants, that neither US nor Israel is party to the Rome Statute, and ASPA 2002; blocks property and suspends entry of designated persons; relies on IEEPA and NEA.

Biden revoked EO 13928 (signed June 2020) on 1–2 Apr 2021; Bensouda and Mochochoko had been designated Sept 2020; Blinken: 'We continue to disagree strongly with the ICC's actions relating to the Afghanistan and Palestinian situations.'
ICC on 7 Feb 2025 'condemns' the order and 'stands firmly by its personnel'.

Designations: Khan with the order (Feb 2025); four judges 5 Jun 2025 (Hohler, Alapini-Gansou, Ibáñez Carranza, Bossa); Albanese 9 Jul 2025; three Palestinian NGOs Sept 2025 (Al Haq, Al Mezan, PCHR); two judges 18 Dec 2025; Rubio: ICC 'an instrument for lawfare'.
20 Aug 2025: Judges Prost (Afghanistan ruling) and Guillou (Netanyahu/Gallant warrants) and Deputy Prosecutors Nazhat Shameem Khan and Mame Mandiaye Niang designated.
June 2026 Judges Prost, Bossa and Alapini-Gansou sued in SDNY claiming the order exceeds IEEPA/NEA authority and violates Fifth Amendment and APA; five earlier suits filed.
Albanese: district court (Judge Leon) on 15 May 2026 preliminarily blocked her sanctions as likely violating free speech; D.C. Circuit stayed that order 22 May; OFAC relisted her 27 May 2026.
Oct 2026: a federal court in Maine refused to dismiss a First Amendment challenge to the ICC sanctions program.

entries.topic: Leahy, UN vetoes, Symington/Glenn and nuclear opacity

claims.text: Leahy laws: 22 USC 2378d (FAA 620M) and 10 USC 362 bar assistance to a unit where there is credible information of a gross violation of human rights; State exception if government 'is taking effective steps to bring the responsible members... to justice'; GVHR vetting focuses on torture, extrajudicial killing, enforced disappearance, rape under color of law.

29 Apr 2024 State found five Israeli units responsible for gross violations (all before Oct 2023, outside Gaza); four 'effectively remediated'; fifth (reportedly Netzah Yehuda) under review; Israeli official 'categorically rejects any attempts to harm the IDF'.
9 Aug 2024 Blinken found Netzah Yehuda violations 'effectively remediated' (soldiers removed, vetting changed, seminar); unit 'can continue receiving security assistance'.

Blaha: ILVF ineligibility decisions rest with Deputy Secretary, 'true for no other country in the world'; Israel may take 'as long as three months' to answer; failed to identify a single ineligible Israeli unit in over four years.

Classified State OIG report (reported Oct 2025) described 'many hundreds' of potential violations by Israeli units in Gaza; review would take 'multiple years'; ILVF needs consensus and Secretary approval; State did not comment.

First US veto on an Israel-related draft: Sunday 10 Sep 1972, Somalia draft on Israeli strikes on Syria and Lebanon after Munich, defeated 13–1–1; Bush cited a 'double standard'. Syria's letter S/10790 (14 Sep 1972).

Al Jazeera (May 2021) counted at least 53 US vetoes of resolutions critical of Israel since 1972 from UN data; AFP counted 46 vetoes on the Palestinian territories as of 18 Sep 2025; 18 Sep 2025 sixth US veto of a Gaza ceasefire demand, 14–1; Ortagus: it 'fails to condemn Hamas or recognise Israel's right to defend itself'.

Symington Amendment (1976; now AECA s.101) bars most aid to a country trafficking in enrichment equipment or technology outside safeguards; Glenn Amendment (1977; AECA s.102(b)) bars aid to non-nuclear-weapon states that detonate a nuclear explosive device; applied to Pakistan 1979 and India/Pakistan 1998.
26 Sep 1969 Nixon–Meir understanding: US ends Dimona inspections and NPT pressure if Israel does not declare, publicize or test; documents not public; Israel never signed NPT.
Military.com (Jan 2026): no administration has made the determination Symington requires; appropriations use 'notwithstanding' language; Glenn not triggered since no known test.
